security_audit.summary: Manual review found that the static detections are false positives from copied CCXT documentation, GitHub page headers, and trading API terminology. No executable scripts, prompt injection, credential exfiltration, hidden filesystem access, or unauthorized network behavior were found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the leading TRANSLATED CONTENT marker before the YAML block so automated scanners can parse metadata cleanly.

remediation.issue: Verbose troubleshooting can expose sensitive data if users paste raw logs
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing API key warning and add clear reminders to redact secrets, account IDs, and private responses before sharing logs.

content.value_statement: Crypto exchange APIs differ across markets, credentials, and order types. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use CCXT reference material correctly.
actual_capabilities: Explains CCXT setup for JavaScript, Python, PHP, C#, Docker, and browser use.
Guides unified exchange methods for market data, orders, balances, funding, and transfers.
Summarizes authentication, API key handling, nonce behavior, and private endpoint requirements.
Covers rate limits, retries, proxies, CORS, and exchange-specific request parameters.
Describes CCXT Pro WebSocket patterns, streaming caches, and watch method behavior.
Helps interpret common errors, missing fields, pagination limits, and exchange capability flags.
limitations: It provides documentation guidance only and does not execute trades for the user.
It cannot guarantee exchange behavior, fees, limits, or availability because exchanges change often.
It does not provide financial advice or assess whether a trade should be placed.
Users must protect API keys and verify all code in sandbox mode before production use.

use_cases.title: Prototype market data access
use_cases.description: Find the right CCXT methods for tickers, order books, trades, candles, and exchange capability checks.

use_cases.title: Debug private API calls
use_cases.description: Review authentication, required credentials, nonce errors, permissions, and private request troubleshooting steps.

use_cases.title: Plan exchange integration behavior
use_cases.description: Compare rate limits, pagination, proxies, WebSocket streams, and exchange-specific parameters before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Find a CCXT method
prompt_templates.prompt: Which CCXT method should I use to fetch current ticker data for one exchange, and what should I check first?

prompt_templates.title: Set up authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to configure CCXT API credentials safely for private balance and order methods.

prompt_templates.title: Debug rate limits
prompt_templates.prompt: My CCXT integration is hitting rate limit and retry errors. Help me inspect the likely causes and safer request patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Design streaming workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CCXT Pro WebSocket workflow for order book and trade streams across multiple symbols, including cache and reconnection concerns.

output_examples.input: How do I fetch market candles with CCXT?
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the unified candle method, explains timestamp and limit behavior, and notes exchange-specific history limits.

output_examples.input: Why does my private order request fail?
output_examples.output: The skill reviews credential setup, required permissions, nonce timing, symbol requirements, and exchange error categories.

output_examples.input: Should I use REST polling or WebSocket streams?
output_examples.output: The skill compares request-response methods with CCXT Pro watch methods, then highlights latency, cache, and subscription tradeoffs.

best_practices: Use sandbox or testnet mode before calling production trading endpoints.
Keep the built-in rate limiter enabled unless you fully control request pacing.
Redact API keys, secrets, verbose logs, account IDs, and withdrawal details before sharing output.
anti_patterns: Do not paste live API keys or secrets into prompts, logs, issues, or examples.
Do not place production orders before validating symbols, amounts, contract sizes, and market type.
Do not disable rate limits or retry failed trading requests without clear idempotency handling.

faq.question: Does this skill place trades?
faq.answer: No. It explains CCXT documentation and implementation patterns. Users control any code execution or trading action.

faq.question: Which languages does the referenced CCXT documentation cover?
faq.answer: The reference material covers JavaScript, Python, PHP, C#, Docker, browser usage, and CCXT Pro WebSocket patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with private exchange APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains credentials, required permissions, nonce behavior, private methods, and common authentication errors.

faq.question: Can it choose profitable trades?
faq.answer: No. It is a coding and documentation skill, not a trading strategy or investment advice tool.

faq.question: How should I handle API keys when using this skill?
faq.answer: Use placeholders in prompts. Store real keys outside prompts, and redact secrets from logs before sharing them.

faq.question: Can it help debug rate limits?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain CCXT rate limit settings, retry behavior, pagination, and request pacing guidance.
